_comment: ADOPT: the institution's binding technology policy (Loom 2.0-rc.8 BrainKit). Ground each entry in an approved source (source-register.json). 'allowed' may be used freely; 'consult' needs the named authority's sign-off; 'forbidden' must not be introduced. Reference the D6 register and supply-chain policy — do not duplicate them. 'radar' (2.2.0) is the LIFECYCLE the three lists lack: assess → trial → adopt → hold, each entry owned and dated, so a technology on trial has a mechanical on-ramp (a `trial` entry is read as `consult` by the develop skill) and a hold has a written reason.

allowed.technology: ADOPT: e.g. the institution's standard language/runtime

forbidden.technology: ADOPT: technology that must not be introduced

standards.standard: ADOPT: binding internal or external standard the institution adopts

registry._comment: ADOPT: the enforcement seam for the lists above. In the Loom the AGENT picks the dependency, so the distinctive risk is not 'a package we chose has a CVE' but 'the agent chose a package nobody approved' — a hallucinated or slopsquatted name that resolves. SCA is structurally bad at this: it tells you a package is vulnerable, not that it should never have been selected. A curated registry closes it by construction — the resolver cannot fetch what the registry does not carry — which turns these lists from a document a reviewer checks into a boundary the build cannot cross. Chainguard Libraries is one instance of the role (Python/Java/JavaScript, built from source); an internal Artifactory/Nexus mirror with an allow-list is another. See ../../loom/references/supply-chain-security.md.

upstream.source: ADOPT: the curated registry URL the resolver is pinned to
upstream.supplier: ADOPT: the role instance (e.g. a hardened-libraries supplier, or your internal mirror)
upstream.fallback_to_public: ADOPT: false — a fallback that silently reaches the public index is not a boundary

resolver_config: ADOPT: the file that pins the resolver, e.g. .npmrc / pip.conf / settings.xml — it belongs to CODEOWNERS, not to the agent
registry.attested_by: ADOPT: the adapter that proves this is live — docs/governance/adapters/<id>.json, reconciled per adapters/README.md

radar._comment: ADOPT: the technology radar — where a technology stands on its way into (or out of) the allowed set. Rings: assess (looking, no use in a governed change), trial (bounded use with the named authority's sign-off — the develop skill treats a trial entry as `consult`), adopt (promoted; also appears in `allowed`), hold (do not start new use; existing use has an exit date). Every entry is owned, dated and grounded; `review_by` is when the ring is re-decided. A radar is a record of decisions, not a wishlist.

entries.authority: ADOPT: who signs off each use while on trial
